name: workflows
runtimeRequirements: Default-loaded through package.json#pi.extensions

saved workflow JavaScript is reviewed trusted input executed by Node's main-context default loader; static node: imports are available under default self-contained-static identity, while local/package/dynamic/source-anchored module behavior requires literal meta.identityCoverage entry-only; either mode can retain host-process filesystem, subprocess, network, and other capabilities, so identity policy, approval metadata, the intended dsl-only authoring convention, and worktrees are not a sandbox
workflow tool accepts name, scriptPath, or legacy script target fields; exactly one must be supplied

workflow semantic input is only optional text of at most 16000 characters; the tool may separately carry closed continuation metadata with one originRunId and 1-8 complete artifact refs, all from that origin, while duplicate identities, unknown fields, malformed refs, object-valued input, and continuation combined with replay-only resumeFromRunId fail before child execution

saved workflow names resolve project .pi/workflows first (canonical), then the additional project directories .claude/workflows and .agents/workflows, then ~/.pi/workflows, then the packaged examples directory extensions/workflows/examples; every directory including that one accepts only the pi-native <name>.workflow.mjs filename, so a foreign host's <name>.js is never resolved and a script authored against another workflow DSL is not portable here; a Package workflow is registered by the existence of its entry file, and a package-boundary test fails when package.json#files does not ship what the directory resolves

curated review and review-fix write their stage prompts inline in the workflow script under one COMMON contract, so the retained script snapshot covers the prompt bytes; review keeps exactly two neighboring resources/*.prompt.md role charters (interrogator, verifier) that are too long to inline, and runtime resolves those from the original workflow source, rejects path and symlink escapes, snapshots bytes once, and records SHA-256 evidence; both entries declare answer counts, id patterns, and string/array bounds in agent({schema}) so a violation is re-asked by the runtime retry instead of ending the run, and bound free-text handoffs with per-call maxAnswerChars; review sends fresh semantic text to a shaped read-only clarifier, either continues or persists exact intent/questions and declares one generic structured operator handoff over those refs, then the host verifies and atomically claims a two-artifact continuation before five bounded coverage-reconciled review stages and runtime-owned review.md with no publisher agent; review-fix receives semantic text plus exactly one host-continuation reference named review.md; the host verifies the successful source run, the full reference, the digest and terminal-projection membership and copies the bytes in before the module starts, and since 2026-07-29 the script neither re-derives that proof nor asserts the bytes came from a Package review verify-review stage, so the operator's closed-continuation choice plus the host's verification of it are what bind the source run, at the accepted residual risk of remediating against another run's review; it asks a no-tool read-only shaped selector for 1-20 id/note/dependency units, rejects invalid ids, notes, edges and cycles, computes stable topological order, runs one writer per selected finding with direct-dependency results, then a host-enforced read-only checker with bounded baseline-frozen repository_check and a fresh dependency-aware re-review; it has no imported helper or publisher, keeps self-contained-static identity, leaves writer changes in the launch checkout, and never commits, pushes, creates a pull request, merges, or deploys

each run owns a canonical .locus/runtime/workflows/<runId>/artifacts/index.json whose records bind runId, artifactId, name, sha256, media type, size, relative path, stage, provenance, and optional source lineage; every agent attempt persists its exact answer, while a fresh child must also contribute its confined Pi transcript and result envelope; replay persists a new answer with replay provenance but fabricates no child evidence; index ownership, path/symlink confinement, duplicate identities, bounded text, transcript headers, and digest reads fail closed; completion projects the newest 20 answer/published refs plus an explicit omitted count into result.json and the native workflow tool result so a later run receives source-truth refs instead of guessing ids, while the full index remains canonical

DSL publishArtifact(name,text) persists deterministic workflow-authored Markdown and returns the complete {runId,artifactId,name,sha256} reference; consumeTextArtifact(ref) accepts only a complete prior-run text reference from an ok source run, verifies identity, media type, size, path and digest, then copies bytes into the current run with source lineage plus verified source target/artifact metadata and its validated terminal string result/ref projection; agent({artifact}) gives the automatic answer record a stable logical name

read-only children may receive repository_check only when explicitly requested; the workflow bridge freezes exact package script commands before any child can write, and the tool accepts exactly one still-matching baseline script name with no arguments or shell text, while the host fixes package-manager argv, timeout, output bound, cwd and cleanup and runs the trusted operator-owned script in a disposable external Git worktree containing current tracked/untracked source bytes; writer-added or modified commands are refused, the operator checkout is never its cwd, and package script execution is not an OS or network sandbox

project-local planning and testing lifecycle examples stay ignored under .pi/workflows; they exercise split-run plan consumption and independent testcase design, implementation/execution, and failure attribution, but are not tracked examples, Package workflows, or public npm package files

at resolution time, existing explicit scriptPath and project saved-name candidates are checked both lexically and by canonical realpath against the canonical project root; an external symlink observed by that check fails before module evaluation, internal symlinks remain allowed after their physical target verifies in-project while the lexical path stays stable as recorded sourcePath, and personal/package sources retain their separate trusted roots; validation and source capture are point-in-time filesystem operations, not a sandbox; legacy script strings normalize to saved names or project-relative paths

each run persists version-2 exact-entry identity with read-only script-<sha256>.workflow.mjs snapshot, scriptSha256, identity policy/coverage, execution source, Node version/platform/arch, sorted builtin imports and unbound dependency descriptions; default self-contained-static rejects recognized direct dependency syntax except literal static node: imports/re-exports and executes the snapshot, while literal top-level meta.identityCoverage entry-only permits local/package/dynamic/require/import.meta behavior through a hash- and run-qualified source URL but labels dependency bytes unbound; createRequire aliases, eval-generated imports and arbitrary host code are outside static analysis and require an honest author downgrade; only old unversioned identity reads as entry-only-legacy, unknown/inconsistent schemas fail closed, structured operator target/identity metadata omits internal paths while runtime error text may contain loader paths, and final snapshot verification follows JSON result detachment before synchronous persistence; hash checks are point-in-time evidence, not an atomic same-owner race guarantee

/workflows run is an explicit operator command: it resolves the launch target, claims one stable session/project background identity with a generation-scoped callback lease, returns the editor while runWorkflowScript continues, and does not pass through model-tool approval or open a second Locus-owned prompt; the programmatic workflow tool remains awaited but registers non-exclusive control with the same owner without occupying the slash-command slot

/workflows run checks the real Pi command context ctx.isIdle before target resolution, transcript creation, or execution; because Pi 0.82.0 invokes extension commands during streaming and would route sendMessage without deliverAs to agent.steer, a busy or unreadable idle state fails closed with a warning, zero sendMessage calls, and zero workflow execution; a second slash run under the same stable session/project identity conflicts until its predecessor settles, while /workflow-stop [runId|last] and compatibility /workflows stop are the sole operator cancellation paths for slash- and tool-launched workflows and report stopping until settlement

first-class /workflow-run, /workflow-stop, /workflow-list, /workflow-info, /workflow-status, and /workflow-continue commands route through the same owners as compatibility /workflows subcommands; Pi native slash filtering and Tab expose the complete names, while command-owned argument completion supplies workflow names, persisted run ids, last, --answer, and replay ids without consuming free-text catalog queries, paths, or semantic input

Pi 0.82.0 is the minimum supported workflow host: all four Pi peer ranges start at 0.82.0, exact development dependencies and lockfile entries use 0.82.0, and tool-origin question projection waits for agent_settled rather than the intermediate turn_end event

actionable awaiting_operator results carry one strict runner-enriched generic handoff envelope over bounded select/text questions, exact terminal artifact refs, origin, and self-contained-static target/script identity; legacy reason-only waits remain readable but not actionable, malformed or forged envelopes fail closed, continuation re-verifies current identity and artifacts, and result.json remains immutable

one source-adjacent atomic claim sidecar excludes parallel continuation across Pi processes, binds to the child run inside the runner, stores no raw answer, releases launch failure, recovers bounded stale pre-start claims, and projects successful/newly-awaiting children as resolved while failed/cancelled children remain retryable

the session-scoped direct-question queue reads durable actionable handoffs oldest-first, shows Question 1 of N without a run picker, and launches at most one continuation; Escape is an answer rather than a postponement — the workflow's continuation receives the question list with an explicit operator-declined note, and each question carries either the answer given before the refusal or a declined marker; nothing reopens automatically except questions published by runs the current Pi session launched, so a new session never raises an older run's question at start or on its first settled turn, while bare /workflows reopens the oldest pending item project-wide, /workflow-continue <runId> opens a named one, and explicit /workflow-stop is the cancellation path

TUI handoffs use one non-overlay inline select/text component shared narrowly with ask, RPC uses native bidirectional extension UI requests, JSON/print requires /workflow-continue with explicit --answer, and embedded child observation remains session.subscribe; Locus serializes its own inline components but Pi exposes no global third-party UI focus lock

/workflows dashboard plus interactive TUI /workflows status and /workflows status <runId> open a persisted disk-only run viewer with run to stage to evidence to content navigation; it groups indexed answers, transcripts, result envelopes, published/consumed text, and journal logs by stage, re-reads and digest-verifies artifacts before rendering, refuses changed, malformed, missing, oversized, or tampered evidence, and owns no live session state

static workflow help, passive list/info/status/detail fallbacks, launch errors, and headless settled receipts use typed operator blocks; interactive TUI /workflows list, info, dashboard, and status use workflow-owned focused custom components, while RPC, print/no-UI, and TUI without custom UI keep bounded static status/detail and the existing live progress panel remains domain-owned
workflow history uses [R] independently from persisted source tags [P]/[U]/[PKG]; passive TUI bounds status/detail to 10/20 rows, RPC to 4/1 rows, and all variants point to persisted run evidence

programmatic workflow tool declares exec approval metadata to the Pi host; approval details warn that the reviewed file has full host Node.js/module access and that approval is consent, not capability isolation
programmatic workflow tool stays headless and does not add a launch prompt
an agent catalog plus the createAgentSession host is required to spawn sub-agents; workflow-local behavior is supplied through rendered prompts

DSL agent/publishArtifact/consumeTextArtifact/continuationArtifacts/parallel/pipeline/phase/log routes every sub-agent through executeAgentRunBoundary with createAgentSdkSessionExecutor; continuationArtifacts exposes readonly exact source refs paired with host-consumed current-run text artifacts; agent() returns exact non-empty child text, automatically persists answer/transcript/result evidence, and parses JSON-looking output only for an opt-in agent({schema}) call
DSL promptFile() renders source-relative .prompt.md resources with strict variables; workflow-local agent files are not supported
DSL workspace() allocates one retained runtime-owned linked worktree at an exact ref and returns an opaque handle that can be reused across agents

workflow agent() live rows compute a workflow parent row id, pass it as live.parentRowId to the SDK executor, and collapse the visible workflow parent row once its real SDK child row exists so the live progress panel and text fallback do not show duplicate Working parent/child rows

workflow agent_end completed, failed, cancelled, and blocked states project to terminal live rows; the shared terminal invariant clears currentTools/currentToolArgs/currentToolStartMs and freezes elapsedMs, while cancelled has its own marker/status, leaves active counts, stops the spinner, and removes the x stop affordance; live-row settlement alone does not decide the script outcome, but a failed/blocked/cancelled result returned directly from parallel() or pipeline() is a typed group failure

workflow live progress uses a pinned passive belowEditor widget while the background lease is active; it projects normalized, stable-deduplicated declared/reached/current stages and one active child through the shared AgentLivePanel, keeps parallel groups as non-selectable headings and round retries in the same slot with rN, then /ps expands the shared fleet for leaf Enter/readable output and Esc/q navigation without abort; explicit workflowRunId provenance removes both the x stop hint and handler for labeled and unlabeled workflow rows, while standalone agent rows retain confirmed x cancellation; session_shutdown immediately disposes the session-owned progress listener and timer even when a runner ignores abort, while terminal/failure cleanup remains idempotent; after completion, input/registered command cleanup or Pi turn_end removes the large presentation while store-owned cleanup retains the newest five workflow run subtrees whose rows are all terminal for /ps viewer, /ps last, and direct guidance; older fully terminal subtrees are pruned, while active, queued, and zero-row runs are not counted or pruned

transcript persistence has an explicit surface mode: a background command run publishes one idle-checked locus-workflow-run boundary banner at launch and then buffers lifecycle with no further active-run sendMessage calls, carrying its originating session generation; after completion a still-current command awaits ctx.waitForIdle, rechecks ctx.isIdle, then immediately appends one visible locus-workflow-run digest with triggerTurn:false and no deliverAs, while session_shutdown/reload revokes stale callbacks and the programmatic tool puts one digest in its native final toolResult

command and tool digests include only bounded workflow/agent lifecycle: lines cap at 160 characters, each run keeps at most 20 agent transitions plus start/final (at most 22 lifecycle lines and 4096 digest characters), raw result/journal data is excluded, journal errors are retained only as fallback text for exactly one final failure with eventKind workflow_end, and workflow agent lines use stable catalog agent plus label rather than a non-canonical parent-row petname

command evidence and digest-persistence warnings use the real Pi warning level; result.json persistence failure is shown once inside the final live/typed result instead of a duplicate toast; if waitForIdle, the final idle check, or sendMessage is unavailable or fails, command digest persistence reports a warning and makes no sendMessage fallback, so it never steers a streaming parent
owned [agent] ->/[agent] <- transport markers are detail-only in /workflows status <runId>; the main status surface suppresses the duplicate markers without suppressing failures or evidence warnings

/workflows list [query] builds one current/history model from the shared first-wins resolver and persisted run index; Project, User, and Package directories are all scanned on every call, so list, info, bare-name run, and unknown-name recovery use one resolver over one set of directories; each selectable row is a two-line block with badge/source/name/description first and an indented exact origin path second, middle truncation preserves path beginning and basename, and very low terminals use a compact one-line fallback; current and run-specific history rows are inspectable, the custom viewer uses all terminal rows except Pi's three footer/status rows with no fixed 24-row ceiling, Pi-native JavaScript highlighting and a persistent top/bottom code frame keep metadata separate while internal scroll reaches the final line, i opens an independently scrollable identity screen where current path or history run id/path/SHA remain reachable with Up/Down, PageUp/PageDown, Home, and End even at terminal widths 8 and 1, Esc/Back returns to the preserved catalog cursor, width-bounded empty/no-match/history-only states have no phantom selection, and RPC/print/no-UI or TUI without custom UI retain an honest passive projection

workflow source actions are editor handoffs: a ready current source offers Back, Start, Edit, and Review; history offers only Back and Review; Tab moves action focus with a caret plus warning color while other actions and metadata labels use semantic success color, Enter resolves the focused typed intent, and only after the shared inline ctx.ui.custom surface completes may the command prefill the restored main editor through setEditorText; Start writes direct /workflows run <resolved-name>, while Edit/Review/diagnosis write Request plus Agent: workflow-author (the bundled .agents/agents/workflow-author.md catalog agent installed with this package) and Additional instructions; no browser action submits editor text, imports or runs a workflow, sends a message, writes a file, or mutates history

history inspection reads only the exact immutable script snapshot persisted for one run; simple run id, lexical run containment, non-symlink directory chain, exact script-<sha256>.workflow.mjs basename, regular non-symlink file type, direct-child realpath containment, readable bytes, valid target, and matching SHA-256 are all required; ready, legacy, missing, unreadable, invalid, and tampered persisted states are explicit, and the browser returns stale if target, path, SHA, or identity coverage changes after catalog selection; no state falls back to current or alternative source

/workflows info [name] builds one source-backed OperatorBlock explaining commands, filesystem precedence, static metadata, trust, DSL primitives, agent catalog selection, model-role metadata, and actual per-call/session model routing; named info resolves through the same first-wins catalog, reports exact source/path, bounded literal meta.description and any declared literal meta.phases, and fails explicitly for unknown names; interactive TUI with custom UI opens a workflow-owned read-only scroll view over that same block, with Up/Down, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End, and Esc/q making the complete semantic contract reachable at 146, 80, and 48 columns; RPC, print/no-UI, and TUI without custom UI retain a bounded passive projection with an honest custom-UI limitation; neither path imports or runs a workflow, invents an execution graph, mutates the editor, or writes files, and this owner-local view does not change generic Ctrl-O, cat, or terminal scrollback

workflow catalog descriptions come only from a bounded static AST scan of top-level literal export const meta, accepting unquoted or quoted literal description keys; listing never executes modules or accepts comments, unrelated description fields, computed metadata, or interpolated descriptions

workflow journal rows use per-kind required and allowed fields before projection, so malformed JSON, empty agent_end, cross-kind fields, invalid counts, and invalid terminal statuses remain explicit diagnostics; a continuation run begins with the exact closed runtime log binding originRunId and sourceRef/consumedRef pairs, whose nested unknown fields, wrong origins/current run ids, duplicate identities, or malformed refs are rejected by readers; dsl.log emits script, internal enter/exit and resume metadata emit runtime, and missing source remains neutral legacy data; child timeout/cancellation waits only a bounded interval for SDK abort acknowledgement before preserving evidence and disposing

workflow live completion prefers result.summary, then scalar result.verdict, then a string result, otherwise reports completed; main TUI, tool, RPC, and headless outputs never dump raw JSON, which stays in status detail and result.json

workflow results cross one JSON-safety boundary: null persists as a valid success; undefined, BigInt, circular, and throwing-toJSON values become an explicit diagnostic sentinel and force the outer persisted envelope to ok:false; a JSON-safe top-level result with ok:false or partial:true is semantic non-success even when a deliberate partial has no error string; mandatory result.json envelope/write failure forces the returned run to ok:false, retains typed resultPersistence evidence, and appends a runtime error journal line so read-side status remains failed

the runner persists one closed disposition beside ok: completed, awaiting_operator, cancelled with operator_stop/session_shutdown/aborted reason, or failed; finish precedence is controlling abort, failed evidence, dsl.awaitOperator declaration, then completed, so a trusted script catch cannot turn an aborted run green; awaitOperator records one bounded last-call-wins declaration with optional generic operatorHandoff without changing the returned payload; all human/model projections consume one strict projector, legacy files without disposition fall back to ok, and malformed/future dispositions or unreadable result envelopes remain unknown

after JSON detach, a script result object with boolean ok:false propagates to the run envelope/status and cannot render as successful; missing or non-boolean ok retains legacy execution-success semantics unless top-level partial:true

semantic failure formatting is owned by workflow-result and shared by transcript, tool/command result blocks, and live progress: technical error wins, otherwise non-empty result summary plus stable unresolvedRows is preserved, with a generic fallback only when neither exists

the packaged benchmarks/weak-model-workflow-v2 evidence surface freezes an exact-baseline seed and identity inputs plus a self-contained adaptive executor/evaluator with embedded oracle/waivers; execute mode validates one approval before any child call, requires exact baseline/seed/red preflight, enforces owner-local sequential writes, fresh focused checker/reviewer/fixer sessions, mandatory replan and fail-closed no-progress/caps, rejects any HEAD change, hashes actual child JSONL, requires matched successful bash receipts including exact npm run check, runs host-owned focused/owner/docs/package checks, and diffs git snapshots around every child before creating independent-harness evidence; caller/model-provided criteria, evidence kinds, refs and digests are ignored, while the AST launch gate permits only audited Node built-ins and rejects local/package imports, re-exports, dynamic imports, and require; it is not a package.json#pi.extensions entry and cannot widen the default runtime surface
workflow run identity is announced before the first journal event so zero-event runs install the same semantic completion surface as eventful runs

workflow live progress and headless liveAgents text fallback render compact rows through the shared local AgentLivePanel contract with source-backed optional metadata only; the generic session viewer labels recorded terminal, cancellation, and failure text without assuming every writer produced an answer, while the workflow adapter alone verifies replay answer artifacts before projection
workflow live rows use the same process-shared store as the agents entrypoint, so active/completed workflow children resolve through petname, last, ids, label, and the focused fleet menu

resumeFromRunId links a fresh workflow run to a prior persisted run summary and replays that run's recorded agent calls; it is not Pi session continuation, and it never reuses the child's side effects, only its recorded answer text. A replayed call also does not re-read: replay is keyed on the request, never on the state the child observed, so a replayed stage answers about the tree as it was when it ran

replay is keyed on each agent attempt's ordinal position plus its fully resolved request (prompt, agent, readOnly, tools, maxToolCalls, model, timeoutMs, maxTurns, label, phase, permissionMode, workspaceMode, workspaceHandle); a declared schema needs no key field because the shape contract is already inside the prompt, and each schema retry is its own recorded attempt. Replay is a strict prefix: the first key mismatch invalidates that call and every later call, including calls whose own prompt is unchanged. A recorded failure keeps its ordinal and always re-runs, and a call resolving to a non-project workspaceMode or carrying a workspaceHandle is never replayed even on a clean key match. The latch fires on key mismatch only, not on a changed outcome: a call that re-runs at a matching key does not break the prefix, so its successors keep replaying answers recorded in a run where that call had a different outcome; because timeoutMs and maxTurns now carry package budget defaults, every record written before those defaults existed fails the key comparison and re-runs rather than serving text a child produced under the SDK host's implicit turn-derived ceiling as though the declared workflow fuse had been in force

replay-safety is scanned by the same AST scan that classifies import edges, never asserted by a meta field: the nondeterministic roots are Date.now, new Date, Math.random, performance.now/timeOrigin, crypto.randomUUID/getRandomValues and process.hrtime/uptime, and the scan folds direct access, computed access, access through globalThis/global/self, a computed global member, a parenthesised constructor, a rebinding of the root (const d = Date, const { random } = Math), and a named, default or namespace import of a nondeterministic node:crypto/node:perf_hooks/node:process export. entry-only coverage is unproven by construction because imported bytes are outside the scan; an unproven script still runs normally but is neither recorded nor replayed. dsl.now() and dsl.random() are the recorded, replayable alternatives

the replay-safety scan is a filter, not a proof: it reads syntax, so access assembled at runtime (globalThis[k] with a computed k, Reflect.get, a root threaded through a parameter), a value smuggled in through process.env or argv, and anything inside an imported module stay invisible to it. The gate that actually prevents a wrong replay is the per-call request key plus the strict prefix latch, which fails closed on any nondeterminism that reaches a prompt or changes call order or count

replay refuses with a named reason written to the journal and result.json — source-run-unusable, script-changed, identity-coverage-unproven, replay-unsafe-script, no-recorded-calls — and every refused or unresolvable call runs for real; no code path fabricates a recorded answer

a run that reused recorded calls is marked as replayed on every surface: replayed:true on agent_start/agent_end journal lines, a typed replay envelope in result.json, replayed=<n> plus a not-fresh-evidence line in /workflows status, [replayed] markers in the status timeline, replayed=<n> in the live progress panel header, and [replayed] plus a replayed count in the bounded command/tool lifecycle digest that enters LLM context; a replayed call reports no usage, so the run budget counts only work that actually happened
bare DSL agent(prompt) defaults to catalog agent default; explicit opts.agent selects another catalog agent and opts.readOnly can impose a host-enforced per-call read boundary

model routing resolves opts.model then opts.modelRole then the agent's frontmatter tier then ctx.model through the host model registry, and the resolved model is what the child session is created with; an unresolvable concrete provider/id selector fails the call by name with no child spawned, an unassigned role degrades to ctx.model and records modelRoleFallback, and agent_end carries executedModel read back from the child session; an agent frontmatter tier written in the pre-tier pi/<role> namespace is read as that role so a catalog copied from an older release still resolves, while pi/<not-a-role> and per-call selectors stay fail-closed

parallel()/pipeline() run through a bounded scheduler seam whose width bounds one call rather than the whole run, so nested fan-out is held instead by the run-wide leaf-agent concurrency gate the budget contract feeds; workspaceMode worktree/temporary-worktree agents receive serialized human approvals and retained per-call git worktrees before child execution

parallel()/pipeline() are fail-closed full barriers for ordinary branch failures: scheduled siblings settle, then a thrown branch/stage or direct return with ok:false or status failed/blocked/cancelled rejects one WorkflowGroupFailureError with stable WORKFLOW_GROUP_FAILURE code, ordered discriminated slots/partialResults, indexed branch and optional stage evidence, and accurate total/completed/failed counts; pipeline stops later stages for a failed item, all-success arrays preserve ordering, fulfilled null remains a successful value distinct from a failed slot, and WorkflowInvocationCapError remains a separate hard run-level failure

an uncaught WorkflowGroupFailureError is projected by the runner into a JSON-safe workflow_group_failure result envelope without branch values and with both inner and outer ok:false; deliberate partial continuation must catch only WORKFLOW_GROUP_FAILURE, rethrow other errors, and return JSON-safe partial:true evidence, which remains semantic non-success; trusted JavaScript can broad-catch, so this is an authoring contract rather than an enforcement boundary

parallel()/pipeline() emit local group_start/group_end journal lines and group live rows with accurate completed/failed barrier counts without adding dynamic fanout, acceptance, async detach, or control semantics
fails closed with an honest reason when the host cannot spawn a child agent session

every attempt of an opt-in agent({schema}) call exposes typed schemaValidation {status:valid|mismatch, attempts, errors} on agent_end, plus source:schema|script on a mismatch when the call declared validate; before any child, the runtime recursively rejects unsupported types/keywords and malformed required/properties/items declarations outside its documented type/enum/required/properties/additionalProperties:false/items/minLength/maxLength/pattern/nonBlank/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems/uniqueTrimmedItems/uniqueBy subset — uniqueItems is restricted to primitive items with uniqueBy as the object route, uniqueTrimmedItems and nonBlank canonicalize with String.prototype.trim, and every misplaced or ill-formed uniqueness declaration is refused with zero child calls, while text options type schema as never so shaped calls cannot return objects under Promise<string>; accepted declarations append a deterministic shape block, validate exact child JSON, retry within SCHEMA_MAX_ATTEMPTS carrying previous errors, count attempts against maxTotalAgentInvocations, and throw SchemaValidationError rather than returning an unshaped or partial value; a child run failure stays WorkflowAgentExecutionError and consumes no schema retry, and plain agent(prompt) keeps the exact-text contract with no parser or prompt augmentation; the optional script callback agent({schema, validate}) runs only on an already schema-valid parsed value, returns string[] whose non-empty result re-asks the child in its own labelled repair block never merged into the schema bullet list, requires schema and a function on both the type and runtime sides, grants one dedicated extra attempt so a validate-declaring call gets 3, refuses a non-array, non-string, Promise, empty-string, over-32 or over-500-character return as a fail-closed run error rather than truncating, propagates an author throw unchanged as a journaled {kind:error, source:script} line consuming no retry, refuses a nested agent() call from inside it, and never joins the canonical request — it is re-applied to replayed answers and a script rejection of a replayed answer fails the run closed instead of re-asking

agent() is the DSL's ONLY model-calling primitive; there is no direct one-shot completion node, no pi-ai completeSimple/streamSimple path, and no llm_start/llm_end/llm_delta journal kind. The run-level token/cost budget shown by /workflows status sums usage from agent_end and from the sole post-child error terminal used when script validation or artifact adoption throws after execution; transport errors that never produced an answer carry no usage

a finished run's terminal text is readable in one step: a prose result is persisted verbatim as result.md beside result.json, the chat digest and the live panel name that file plus the exact command, and /workflows result [runId|last] opens the whole untruncated text in a scrollable read-only screen while a host without custom UI gets a bounded preview plus the exact path; structured results stay in result.json, a run recorded before result.md existed is recovered from the persisted envelope, and both /workflows result and /workflows status accept the short run suffix every surface prints, last, or a full run id, and a suffix matching several runs is reported with the real match count plus the listed candidates instead of opening the wrong run or reading as not found

every workflow run is bounded by one package budget contract (DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_BUDGET) that the runner applies without the script declaring anything: global leaf-agent concurrency 4 across nested groups, 200 total agent() invocations, a 7200000 ms wall clock over the agent chain, and per child 600000 ms, 1000 tool calls, 5 turns and 500000 answer characters; the run-level axes concurrency/totalAgents/runtimeMs are overridable only through the host-side RunWorkflowScriptOptions.budget and by nothing a *.workflow.mjs can reach, while maxToolCalls, timeoutMs, maxTurns and maxAnswerChars are per-call agent() options where a narrowing is silent and a raise emits a runtime-source journal line naming axis, default and requested value; the run deadline is checked when a child STARTS, so a run is bounded by runtimeMs plus at most one child's own timeoutMs while script code that calls no further agent is not bounded by it; the SDK host's per-child turn budget is derived from the declared timeoutMs so the workflow-level timeout failure always precedes it; every run journals the applied budget, and .locus/runtime/workflows/<runId>/logs/README.md prints each axis against gate-owned peak concurrency, agent invocations, run wall clock, longest child and observed tokens, printing per-child tool calls, turns and answer characters as not recorded and cost as unavailable rather than zero, with tokens and cost reported and never enforced; a replayed call spends one invocation against totalAgents and starts no child, so it is labelled as replayed there and excluded from the longest-child duration and the observed tokens, and a run served entirely from records reports its longest child as not recorded
stateUsed: .locus/runtime/workflows/<runId>/result.md — the verbatim text of a prose terminal result, written beside result.json and opened by /workflows result
.locus/runtime/workflows/<runId>/operator-handoff-claim.json when an actionable handoff is claimed; mutable claim metadata never becomes an artifact and never stores the answer
.locus/runtime/workflows/<runId>/artifacts/index.json plus answers, fresh child transcripts/result envelopes, workflow-published text, and verified prior-run input copies
uncommitted source changes in the operator launch checkout when review-fix applies an agent-selected validated finding DAG from one immutable continued review.md
